narr: Two rounds of heavy rainfall affected Northern Alabama and Southern Middle Tennessee, with the first round producing widespread river flooding across the area. In addition, flash flooding occurred in several locations with the first event, and again with the second event just 48-72 hours later. While most river gage locations fell back below flood stage by the end of the week, the Tennessee River at Florence lingered above flood stage through February 19th.
ev: Portions of Douglas Road reported underwater due to flash flooding. Depth of water was about 6 to 8 inches in depth.
Robinson Creek Road was underwater due to flash flooding. Depth of water was between 8-10 inches.
Barkley Bridge Road between 55 and West Lacon Road was reported flooded. Depth of water about a foot deep.
Portions of Piney Grove Road between Douglas Road and Highway 31 were flooded. Depth of water unknown.
CR 1711 between 1727 and Brooklyn Road was reported impassable due to flash flooding. Depth of water estimated to be about 7 or 8 inches deep.
Dekalb County EMA reports a bridge washed out and the road closed on CR 1986.
Flash flooding reported on Six Mile Creek Road near Florette. Depth of water at least 4-6 inches at this time.
Widespread flash flooding on CR 565 between Hanceville to Dodge City reported by Cullman County EMA. Depth of water between 6-10 in some spots.
A portion of River Loop Road between Cold Stream Road and McCutcheon Loop Road was reported flooded by Morgan County EMA. Depth of water was about 8-10 inches.

Corrects previous Flash Flood report from 5 ENE South Vinemont. CR 1427 between 1428 and 1422 was flooded and partially damaged by flood waters. Depth of water estimated to be about a foot or more deep.
CR 61 at Hwy 71 was reported flooded. Depth of water estimated to be 6-8 inches.
CR 491 south of Hwy 117 near Stevenson was reported flooded. Depth of water about 8-10.
Flash flooding reported on New Cut Road near Massey. Depth of water estimated to be 6-8 inches in depth.
